hypotheses_falsified.claim: Issuing the next-layer prediction to the store is always worth it.
hypotheses_falsified.evidence: With routing replayed from a Zipf(1.1) trace (which the synthetic router cannot predict) 94% of prefetches were wasted: 119 GB read for 128 tokens vs 29 GB without prefetch, 6.15 vs 13.45 tok/s. Fix: every prediction is scored against the next layer's actual experts (EWMA of precision) and handed to the store only while precision >= 0.5 * top_k / (top_k + prefetch_extra). After the fix: replay 13.4-13.8 tok/s (= prefetch-off level, 0 prefetches issued), synthetic greedy case unchanged at 11.0-11.2 tok/s with 92% precision. Output never depends on it.

hypotheses_falsified.claim: Per-(token, head) attention, each head streaming its KV rows with portable dot16, is adequate.
hypotheses_falsified.evidence: Long-context decode was 13.6 tok/s at 3000 positions vs 23 at short context, and MLA would stream the shared latent cache once per head (128x for DeepSeek). Replaced by the shared-row passes (see validated hypotheses).

hypotheses_falsified.claim: hearth_open may reset the process-wide log level to WARN when verbose = 0.
hypotheses_falsified.evidence: It undid the embedding application's (and test's) own hx_set_log_level, flooding test output with expected store warnings. Now only HEARTH_LOG sets the level, and verbose 1/2 only raise it.

open_questions: Prefetch precision on real models is unknown: synthetic make_shaped weights give 92% (residual stream barely changes between random layers), replayed traces give ~6% (unpredictable by construction). Measure with a converted real model; PF_MIN_PREC = 0.5 is a guess.

Hit rates on make_shaped containers with greedy decoding are inflated: tok_embd rows come from 97-row pools and greedy argmax repeats tokens (27 distinct of 48). Use --replay with a recorded or hearth.sim trace for cache studies.
The engine-vs-reference bit-exactness on Q8/Q4 containers (max error 0.0) is a strong regression signal but lives only in a scratch script; tests/py (T03/T07 owners) could assert it.

Attention value sums (o = sum_t p_t v_t, sequential in t) run in portable C (SSE2 by MSVC); with an elementwise canonical axpy in hx_kernels they could use AVX-512 (see contract_issues). Prefill at 3000 tokens is 74% attention.
At long context the F32 KV cache dominates: ~576 MB/token of reads at 3000 positions for Qwen3-30B-A3B; an opt-in F16/BF16 KV (INV-LOSSLESS-DEFAULT: opt-in, measured) would halve it.
Pool spin 1000 us was ~2% faster than 100 us on the I/O-bound replay benchmark (two runs each, noisy); revisit on a quiet machine.
DeepSeek-V3 / Kimi-K2 shaped benchmarks (MLA at 128/64 heads, C=512) were not run; MLA is verified for correctness only on tiny containers (4 and 20 heads).
